forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {見捨|みす}てていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to abandon, to forsake, to desert
definitions.explanation: To give up on someone or something and leave them without help or care. Carries a strong emotional connotation of betrayal or cold-heartedness.

examples.japanese: ⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{見捨|みす}てるわけ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧はいかない。
examples.english: I can't just abandon my friend.

examples.japanese: ⟦{困|こま}っている→困る：00861_komaru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{見捨|みす}てないでほしい。
examples.english: Please don't turn your back on people in trouble.

examples.japanese: ⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{倒産|とうさん}→倒産：03452_tousan⟧しそう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{社員|しゃいん}→社員：03065_shain⟧たち⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{次々|つぎつぎ}→次々：03522_tsugitsugi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{見捨|みす}てて{辞|や}めていった。
examples.english: When the company was on the verge of bankruptcy, the employees deserted one after another.

notes:
USAGE:
{見捨|みす}てる is a compound verb from ⟦{見|み}→見る：00283_miru⟧ (see) and ⟦{捨|す}てる→捨てる：00892_suteru⟧ (to throw away). It implies a deliberate decision to stop caring about or helping someone. The phrase {見捨|みす}てるわけ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧はいかない (I can't just abandon...) is very common and expresses moral obligation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見捨|みす}てるわけ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧はいかない: can't just abandon
- {見捨|みす}てられる: to be abandoned/forsaken (passive)
- {見捨|みす}てないで: don't abandon me/us
- ⟦{神|かみ}→神：02147_kami⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{見捨|みす}てられる: to be forsaken by God
